digest: A multi-stage incident involving phishing delivery, encoded PowerShell script execution, and Cobalt Strike C2 beaconing from workstation WS-FIN-09. Evidence includes endpoint process execution, network beaconing, and threat intelligence corroboration.

evidence_findings.title: Initial Execution via Malicious Document
evidence_findings.subject: WS-FIN-09
evidence_findings.evidence: Process logs show 'excel.exe' spawning 'powershell.exe' on host 'WS-FIN-09' (10.20.4.115).
evidence_findings.conclusion: Execution of a malicious document led to the initial compromise of the workstation.

evidence_findings.title: Encoded PowerShell Command Execution
evidence_findings.subject: powershell.exe
evidence_findings.evidence: The 'powershell.exe' process executed with '-NonI -W Hidden -EncodedCommand <BASE64_PAYLOAD>'. Deobfuscation revealed an attempt to download a payload from a remote domain.
evidence_findings.conclusion: An encoded PowerShell command was used to download and execute a secondary payload, indicating defense evasion.

evidence_findings.title: Command and Control Beaconing Detected
evidence_findings.subject: 10.20.4.115 to 198.51.100.44
evidence_findings.evidence: Firewall logs show persistent outbound TLS session from '10.20.4.115' (WS-FIN-09) to '198.51.100.44' on port 443, with periodic 30-second interval pulses.
evidence_findings.conclusion: WS-FIN-09 established a persistent C2 communication channel.

evidence_findings.title: Malicious C2 Infrastructure Identified
evidence_findings.subject: stage2.malicious-domain.xyz
evidence_findings.evidence: The domain 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz' (198.51.100.44) is identified as malicious, resolved via Fast Flux DNS, has a high malicious reputation score (89/100), and matches a US-CERT advisory bulletin.
evidence_findings.conclusion: The observed network communication is directed towards known malicious command and control infrastructure.

attack_chain.description: Phishing email delivery led to a user opening a malicious attachment on WS-FIN-09.
A malicious Excel document executed an encoded PowerShell command on the endpoint.
The PowerShell command used '-EncodedCommand' and '-W Hidden' to obfuscate its true intent and evade detection.
The PowerShell script downloaded and executed a payload, establishing a persistent TLS C2 beacon to 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz'.

attack_timeline.attack_behavior: Suspicious process execution (excel.exe spawning powershell.exe) detected on WS-FIN-09.
Outbound beacon traffic to an untrusted subnet detected from WS-FIN-09.
Host WS-FIN-09 network isolation approved by SOC Lead.

ioc_indicators.context: C2 beacon destination, identified as malicious via TI and US-CERT advisory.
C2 beacon destination IP, associated with malicious domain.
Malicious encoded PowerShell execution on endpoint WS-FIN-09.

remediations.description: Isolate host WS-FIN-09 from the network to prevent further C2 communication and lateral movement.
Block 'stage2.malicious-domain.xyz' and '198.51.100.44' at network perimeter firewalls and DNS resolvers.
Conduct a full forensic analysis of WS-FIN-09 to identify initial infection vector, persistence mechanisms, and extent of compromise.
Search for similar encoded PowerShell executions or C2 beaconing activity across the environment to identify other potentially compromised systems.

unknowns: The specific content or filename of the initial phishing attachment.
The identity of the user who opened the malicious attachment.
The exact payload delivered by the C2 server and its full capabilities.
Whether the C2 activity led to further compromise or data exfiltration.
The full scope and objectives of the APT activity mentioned in the case tags.
